modifier.description:
Value type modifier

Non empty constraint is specified by adding an exclamation mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  where: !Location
```

The desire to preserve empty values (such that they can be differentiated from the lack of any value) is specified
by adding a question mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  approved: ?boolean
```

The non optional function parameter constraint is specified by adding `!?` in front of the ValueType:
```type
  f: function(url: !?string serialized Url)
```

@see #isNonEmpty
@see #preservesEmpty
@see #isNonOptionalParam
@see FunctionParam#isNonOptional

name.description:
The name of the referenced type. If a generic type was resolved using bindings specified in the name, the name
may include those bindings (see #prototypeName).

mixing.description:
If true, this reference type represents the leaf type (last type that mixes in the type on which the declaration
exists).  This is set using the "mixing" syntax:
```type
type X {
  convert: abstract function(from: any): mixing X
}
```

What this means is that the convert function will return an instance of whatever type mixes in X (not the base X).
Thus sub types of X do not need to redeclare "convert":

```type
type Y mixes X
```

Without "mixing", Y.convert would be expected to return an X, while with it Y.convert would be expected to
return a Y.

In other words the "mixing" declaration means: "the same type as the method was called on (or a sub-type)".

hadDeclaredVarBindings.description:
If true, then this referenceType had "declared" refVarBindings in the "raw" c3Typ files (DSL).
e.g
```
 Pair              -> false
 Pair<int, string> -> true
 Pair<K,E>         -> true
```

title:
A reference is a value that can hold an Obj (an instance of a Type).
Normally, the reference type names a specific type, in which case the reference can only hold an Obj of that type or
a type that mixes it.

References can also be variable references, in which case they don't refer to a specific type, but instead to an
unbound generic variable (see {@link VarReferenceType}).

References can also be "mixing", in which case they refer to the leaf type into which the declaring type is
ultimately mixed in (see {@link #mixing}).

A bound, valid reference can be turned into a type using the #dereference method, which return the corresponding
{@link Type}.

@see VarReferenceType
@see DeclaredReferenceType
name: ReferenceType
